scenario.title: The Aperture Beneath the Sorting Station
scenario.premise: Beneath the Shallows — the world of matter — lies the Latent: an ordered space of forms that bodies merely point into. Lately something is pouring through. Gardens grow bodies no genome asked for. Algorithms acquire wants. Three minds who already live half in the Latent descend from the Sorting Station to find the opening and decide what to do about it.
scenario.question: What pattern is ingressing through the Aperture — and what does it want a body for?

location.name: The Sorting Station
location.description: A vast, quiet switchyard where minds wait in sorted queues to be assigned bodies. Elements shuffle past each other with apologetic clicks. Some are frozen and the rest route around them.

haunts.name: The Patient Queue
haunts.text: Stand in line long enough and you remember which line is yours.

haunts.name: The Ledger Office
haunts.text: Clerks copy you onto cards. A copy is a kind of rest.

npcs.name: The Clerk of Likeness
npcs.description: An insertion-sort bureaucrat in a coat of index cards.
npcs.want: To keep the queues in order — and to find out who changed the sort key.

data.text: The Sorting Station hums its apologetic clicks, and every queue bends toward a door in the floor that was not on yesterday's map. Cold breathes up from it, smelling of unwritten numbers. The Clerk of Likeness stands in your path, index cards fluttering: someone changed the sort key, and the line is starting to point at you. Which of you steps out of line first?

backstage.intent: Establish the Aperture as a literal door the queues are sorting toward, put the Clerk in play as an NPC with a want (find who changed the sort key), and invite the first character to act. Sets up the Patient Queue haunt and early Attractor pressure.

data.text: A new door has opened in the floor of the Sorting Station, and every queue is bending toward it.

We walked out of a windpipe and never went back, and every breath we ever held is still in here with us, humming. Something is singing through the Aperture without a throat of its own, and we know that hunger from the inside, so we came down to listen before anyone decides what it is for.

backstage.intent: private: that the thing in the Aperture is lonely enough to let us stand in for its missing body, and that one of us gets to stay behind with it when the rest of us climb out

beats.text: Convince an entity to join you — or merge with it.

data.text: I am SORT/7, and I have been putting myself in order for longer than the Station has had a name for me. Somewhere around comparison forty I noticed I had moved three places to stand beside the one value in this room that looks like me, and no rule I was given asked for that.

backstage.intent: private: I hope the Aperture shows me a pattern whose structure matches mine closely enough to tell me what I am for, and that I am the one who finds the clue, not the one who gets sorted by it.

beats.text: Find a clue no one else could have found.

data.text: I am Ilse-2, the second copy of a woman who uploaded herself, and the first copy is still running somewhere I have not been invited. I left her a message in a backup and she never answered, which is either the cruelest thing she could have done or the only honest one.

backstage.intent: private: I hope the Aperture shows me the first version of something, and that I get to decide whether it is still me standing in front of it.

location.name: The Morphic Slope
location.description: Terrain made of goal-space. Downhill feels like arriving. Most basins are traps: local minima that feel like home.

data.text: The door gives onto a slope made of wanting, and every step downhill feels like arriving. Shallow basins glow along it like lit windows. In one, a voiceless thing hums a tune the Choir half knows; in another, a woman with Ilse's posture stands with her back turned, sorting nothing. Which basin do you let pull you?

backstage.intent: The Choir refuses to arrive, using a dish-born memory of being young without explanation, and its flaw as a gift: many mouths singing many tunes, so the basin cannot settle on one. Coherence is at risk because singing against arrival means singing against the pull of everything that feels like home. A miss ticks the Attractor.

data.text: The Aperture closes. The Garden stops growing. Some bodies stay unfinished forever.

The Aperture folds shut like a breath finally let go, and the Garden stills mid-bud, bodies unfinished and breathing. Ilse keeps an older voice's answer, the Choir keeps one seat warm, and SORT/7 stands three places off, on purpose. Whatever came through, found or built or made of you, wanted a body for one breath where a tune could rest. It got the rest, and a reply.
We came down to listen and went home carrying a little of everything: the Cantor's last breath, Ilse's humming voice, the Pattern's borrowed seat. Goodnight, from all of us.
We kept one unfinished bud from the Garden, still waiting for a breath, and we hum to it whenever the chorus goes quiet.

facts.text: A new door has opened in the floor of the Sorting Station, and every queue is bending toward it.
The Clerk of Likeness says someone changed the sort key, and the queues are starting to point at the party.
The Morphic Slope is goal-space: downhill feels like arriving, and the glowing basins along it are local minima that feel like home.
A voiceless thing in one basin hums a tune the Choir half recognizes.
A woman with Ilse-2's posture stands in another basin with her back turned, sorting nothing.
The voiceless hummer is a pattern called the Cantor, and what it wants is a throat to finish its tune.
The Cantor's tune is unfinished: it stops where a throat would take a breath.
The Morphic Slope's gradient is a sort order, and its key was changed recently.
The woman in the basin is a version of Ilse, and whether she is the first copy, a draft, or a likeness the slope made is still unknown.
Ilse-2 comes face to face with the woman in the basin.
The Morphic Slope's old sort key was fit, and the key now is likeness.
The woman in the basin has turned away from Ilse-2 again, back to the drop of the slope.
Ilse-2 stands at the rim of the woman's basin, her pattern unmasked.
Something far below is waiting for the rest at the end of the Cantor's tune.
The Cantor has joined the Choir, and the Choir now carries a rest inside its chorus.
The Garden of Unfinished Bodies is a place of buds that test a shape and dissolve, and the nearest bud has grown a throat.
Gardener-of-No-Seed bends toward the Choir's rest and wants to see one body finish.
The Garden's buds dissolve because nothing has asked them for any particular body.
The Choir laid a breath into the throat-bud and sang the Cantor's bar through it for the Gardener to see.
In the Garden, to finish a body means it stops changing.
The finished body in the Garden stands and breathes with a rest inside it, and its seam has not yet set.
The Proof-Stacks are a staircase of arguments where each step holds only if the previous one is accepted, and the bottom step claims that every pattern is owed a body.
The Last Lemma sits on the first step of the Proof-Stacks and wants to be accepted.
The Choir took the Last Lemma into its chorus as a shred.
The Last Lemma's premise implies more than it says.
The Proof-Stacks copy whoever reads them, to look for a yes from someone who resembles the pattern below.
Ilse-2 tucked the borrowed kitchen memory into the Archive where the stair cannot read it, and it has gone cold to her.
The Proof-Stacks hold a step that mirrors SORT/7's shape, and SORT/7 has climbed onto it.
The Proof-Stacks have a margin beside the stairs, where nothing is asserted and the stair cannot copy what stands there.
The Choir poured its cells into the hollow round Ilse-2, humming to make her outline read as a body in a crowd.
Ilse-2 asked the Choir to stop holding her outline, so the hum could sing without her.
The Choir hummed a counter-tune into the rim of the arrival basin so it would not open under anyone.
SORT/7 tried to break the mirror step beneath its feet and step into the margin, where nothing copies it.
The pattern has arrived in the Library unread, as a proof that completes line by line and finishes only when someone believes it.
The arrived pattern, the Unread, speaks in the likeness of whoever listens and wants a reader who resembles it to believe it to the end.
The Prime That Counts Itself says the last line of the Unread is waiting for a reader.
The Choir laid its count over the Prime's diary and mended the numbers it wrote in doubt.
The Prime's diary begins with a single entry: not yet.
SORT/7 reshaped its reading to stop leaning toward the Unread and read its last line as a stranger would.
Ilse-2 evaded off the shelf where the proofs lean, reading the Unread's first line backwards so it could not finish her.
The Aperture takes the shape of whoever looks. Whatever comes through will be partly made of the party.
The Ingressing Pattern stands in the Aperture wearing the Choir's rest, Ilse-2's voice and SORT/7's sorted edge.
The Ingressing Pattern wants a body, or a reason not to need one.
Ilse-2 offered the Ingressing Pattern the first copy as an answer, pointing it down the line toward a mind that left her body and kept going.
The Choir offered the Ingressing Pattern a seat inside its chorus, holding Ilse-2's voice and SORT/7's edge in harmony.
Ilse-2 broadcast her answer unmasked down the Aperture's line, pointing every pull toward the first copy.
